investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-04T12:36:13Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production API's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at the /v1/agents endpoint. Because the failure occurs before any agent is provisioned, zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable. This is an eval-detected infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency of the production-api remote-agent provisioning path; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning service — was unreachable from the production API at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check routes through POST /api/agents → swarm gateway ELB → /v1/agents, so a connectivity or availability failure at the gateway layer causes a 502 on all three checks simultaneously with the same error message. The root cause is most likely a swarm gateway availability or routing problem (ELB unhealthy, target group drained, security-group rule change, or DNS resolution failure) rather than an application code defect, because the error is returned before any provisioning logic executes and is identical across all sibling checks.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 has no healthy targets (target group fully drained, instances crashed, or deployment in progress) — highest evidence strength given the 502 bad_gateway code and ~10 s latency before failure.

Network-level connectivity loss between the production API and the ELB (security group rule change, VPC routing change, or NACLs blocking egress to the ELB) — consistent with the 'error sending request' phrasing which suggests a transport-layer failure.
DNS resolution failure for the ELB hostname causing the production API to be unable to establish a TCP connection to the swarm gateway — would also produce the observed error message.
Swarm gateway service itself is down or restarting (e.g., a deployment of the /v1/agents service) — would cause the ELB to return 502 if all backend instances are unhealthy.

Transient eval-run-time blip in the swarm gateway (brief restart, rolling deploy) — lower confidence because all three sibling checks failed sequentially across a ~32-second window (12:36:13 to 12:36:45), suggesting the outage persisted rather than being a momentary spike.

The root cause is most likely a missed, failed, or skipped GitHub Actions workflow run that publishes status.json.
